questions.stem: A particle of mass m moving with velocity v collides with a stationary particle of mass 2m. After collision, they stick together and continue to move together with velocity
questions.solution: Applying conservation of linear momentum: $mv + 2m\times0 = (3m)v' \Rightarrow v' = \dfrac{v}{3}$

In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensities at two points, for the path difference $\frac{\lambda}{4}$ and $\frac{\lambda}{3}$ ($\lambda$ being the wavelength of light used) are $I_1$ and $I_2$ respectively. If $I_0$ denotes the intensity produced by each one of the individual slits, then $\dfrac{I_1 + I_2}{I_0} = \ldots$
questions.solution:
$I = 4I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\Delta\phi}{2}\right)$

For path difference $\frac{\lambda}{4}$: $\Delta\phi = \frac{\pi}{2}$, $I_1 = 4I_0\cos^2\frac{\pi}{4} = 2I_0$

For path difference $\frac{\lambda}{3}$: $\Delta\phi = \frac{2\pi}{3}$, $I_2 = 4I_0\cos^2\frac{\pi}{3} = I_0$

$\therefore \dfrac{I_1 + I_2}{I_0} = 3$

questions.stem: A thermodynamic system is taken through cyclic process. The total work done in the process is :

questions.stem: The effect of increase in temperature on the number of electrons in conduction band $(n_e)$ and resistance of a semiconductor will be as:
questions.solution: As temperature increases, more electrons are excited to the conduction band, conductivity increases and therefore resistance decreases.

questions.stem: A 12.5 eV electron beam is used to bombard gaseous hydrogen at room temperature. The number of spectral lines emitted will be:
questions.solution: The electron can transfer up to 12.09 eV, exciting hydrogen to $n = 3$. Number of spectral lines $= \dfrac{3(3-1)}{2} = 3$

questions.stem: At any instant the velocity of a particle of mass 500 g is $(2t\hat i + 3t^2\hat j)\ \text{ms}^{-1}$. If the force acting on the particle at $t = 1$ s is $(\hat i + x\hat j)$ N. Then the value of x will be:
questions.solution: $\vec a = 2\hat i + 6t\hat j$; at $t = 1$, $\vec a = 2\hat i + 6\hat j$. $\vec F = 0.5(2\hat i + 6\hat j) = \hat i + 3\hat j$. Hence $x = 3$

questions.stem: In a reflecting telescope, a secondary mirror is used to:

options.text: reduce the problem of mechanical support
move the eyepiece outside the telescopic tube

questions.solution: The secondary mirror reflects light out of the tube to the eyepiece. It has the advantage of a large focal length in a short telescope.
